title: Daily prayer
hook: a set time and place for prayer
tomorrow: what's Sunday for, if it's not just the day before Monday?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: what works. The rule for life starts with an inventory, not a list of new demands. First piece: prayer, and the question of when.

The alarm goes off, and before your feet touch the floor you've read three messages and one piece of bad news. Morning gets claimed fast. So does night. Ask people who pray and you'll hear two camps. Some say pick a time and a place and never move it. Others say that's too rigid: real prayer happens anywhere, in the car, at the sink. Both camps can quote the Bible.
screen: `THE MORNING GETS CLAIMED.` → `TWO CAMPS.` → `BOTH QUOTE THE BIBLE.`

segments.voice: Camp one: same time, same place. A psalm says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Seven times a day I have given praise to thee." Daniel kneels by his window toward Jerusalem three times a day, even when it's against the king's law. Jesus says, "enter into thy chamber, and having shut the door, pray to thy Father in secret." The best case: a set time doesn't depend on mood. On flat days, the habit carries you. Camp two: anytime, anywhere. Paul writes three words: "Pray without ceasing." Brother Lawrence, a Carmelite brother who worked in a monastery kitchen, said the noise and clatter of his kitchen didn't keep him from God any more than kneeling did. The best case: if prayer happens only at seven, God becomes an appointment. The Church's own practice holds both. The Liturgy of the Hours sets prayer at fixed points from morning to night, so the whole day between them can become prayer. The fixed times are the fence posts; the rest is the field. The Angelus does both at once: a short prayer traditionally said morning, noon and evening, a fixed time that interrupts whatever you're doing.
screen: `CAMP ONE: SAME TIME, SAME PLACE.` · `CAMP TWO: PRAY WITHOUT CEASING.` · `THE HOURS HOLD BOTH.` · then, large: `FENCE POSTS, THEN THE FIELD.`

segments.voice: Choose your time and your place, out loud or on paper: this chair, this hour. Then sit there now, in that spot if you can, and spend the two minutes simply arriving. Nothing to say yet; just learn where it is.
Daily prayer. A set time and a set place, so prayer doesn't depend on mood, and the rest of the day can fill in.
Your line: same time, same place. Fence posts first; the field fills in. Talk tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics pray at set times, such as morning and evening prayer, grace at meals, the Angelus, or the Liturgy of the Hours, and also pray short prayers through the day.
